html:
infra — the swesim hosted stack on GCP

Terraform for everything that runs swesim in production: Cloud Run worker pools (one per Temporal task queue) and the IAP-protected console, the GCS bucket that is the record, Cloud SQL for the rebuildable index, Secret Manager, the two service accounts, Workload Identity Federation for GitHub Actions, and a little logging. Temporal Cloud and Modal are external (their addresses are variables; their credentials are secrets). Nothing project-specific is in a tracked file: the project id, accounts, bucket names and hostnames are variables with neutral defaults.

Binding documents: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-13-hosted-pipeline-brief.md (§2, §9) and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-13-interfaces.md (§9, the infra ⇄ code contract).

What exists after make cloud-bootstrap

Piece Resource Notes
Image registry Artifact Registry swesim (Docker) in <region> <region>-docker.pkg.dev/<project>/swesim/worker:<sha7> and :latest; workloads are pinned to the digest. Cleanup: keep 20 most recent, delete untagged after 30 days.
The record Bucket swesim-<project>-workspace Versioned, uniform access, public access prevented; noncurrent versions pruned (keep 5 / 30 days). Mounted at /workspace read-write on the pools and the trial Jobs, read-only on the console (uid=1000,gid=1000 mount options match the image's user).
Build sources Bucket <project>_cloudbuild Where gcloud builds submit stages sources; objects expire after 7 days.
Terraform state Bucket <project>-swesim-tfstate Created by scripts/cloud/bootstrap.sh (outside Terraform, by design); versioned. Also holds env.auto.tfvars.json for the GitHub deploy workflow.
Index Cloud SQL Postgres 16 swesim-index-<4hex> db-custom-2-7680, zonal, SSD, daily backups + PITR. Public IP with no authorized networks: reachable only through the Cloud Run Cloud SQL connection (/cloudsql/<connection_name> unix socket, IAM-authenticated proxy). Database swesim, user swesim.
Secrets Secret Manager TEMPORAL_API_KEY SWESIM_WORKER_SECRET ANTHROPIC_API_KEY OPENAI_API_KEY OPENROUTER_API_KEY GH_TOKEN MODAL_TOKEN_ID MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET — resources by Terraform, values only by scripts/cloud/push_secrets.py. DB_PASSWORD and SWESIM_DATABASE_URL (postgresql+psycopg://swesim:<pw>@/swesim?host=/cloudsql/<conn>) are the only Terraform-written versions.
Identity swesim-worker Runtime identity of pools, Jobs, console: secretmanager.secretAccessor per secret, storage.objectAdmin on the bucket, cloudsql.client, run.developer (creates/executes/deletes trial Jobs), iam.serviceAccountUser on itself, log/metric writer.
swesim-deployer CI identity: viewer, run.admin, cloudbuild.builds.editor, artifactregistry.writer on the repo, secretmanager.viewer (names) + secretAccessor on TEMPORAL_API_KEY, DB_PASSWORD, SWESIM_DATABASE_URL only, storage.objectAdmin on the state and build buckets, storage.objectUser on the record, serviceAccountUser on swesim-worker and itself.
WIF pool github / provider github-oidc Trusts token.actions.githubusercontent.com for assertion.repository == <github_repository> only; that principal set may impersonate swesim-deployer.
Compute Worker pools swesim-authoring, swesim-build, swesim-trials, swesim-control Same image, SWESIM_TASK_QUEUE=<pool name>, 1 vCPU / 2 GiB, manual instance counts (pool_instances), bucket + Cloud SQL volumes, secrets as env references.
Service swesim-console Same image, command uvicorn swesim.dashboard.app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080, Cloud Run native IAP (iap_enabled, ingress all): the IAP service agent holds run.invoker, iap_members hold iap.httpsResourceAccessor. Only TEMPORAL_API_KEY, SWESIM_WORKER_SECRET, SWESIM_DATABASE_URL are mounted (no provider keys).
Observability Log metrics swesim/trial_reconcile, swesim/worker_crashes; alert "swesim worker crash loop" The alert is a log-match condition on worker-pool container exits (rate-limited to one notification per 30 min per pool); notification_channels is empty by default (the alert exists, nobody is paged).
Not Terraform Jobs swesim-trial-<id> Created at runtime by the Cloud Run launcher (swesim/workflows/launchers/cloudrun.py), one per trial, deleted after the record is written.

Environment on the pools/console follows interfaces §9 exactly (SWESIM_WORKSPACE=/workspace, SWESIM_REGISTRY, SWESIM_BUCKET, SWESIM_TRIAL_LAUNCHER=cloudrun, SWESIM_ORIGIN=cloudrun, SWESIM_WORKER_IMAGE_DIGEST, SWESIM_GCP_PROJECT/REGION, SWESIM_EVALUATORS, SWESIM_SPEND_CAP_USD, SWESIM_STAKEHOLDER_URL, SWESIM_CONSOLE_URL, SWESIM_IAP_AUDIENCE, TEMPORAL_ADDRESS, TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE); empty values are omitted so Settings sees "unset".

Variables (infra/variables.tf)

Variable Default Meaning
project — (required) GCP project id
region us-central1 Region for everything
image "" → <artifact_repo>/worker:latest Digest reference the pools/console run; make deploy passes the digest
iap_members [] IAM members allowed through IAP (user:..., group:...)
iap_programmatic_clients [] Opt-in, organization OAuth clients only: client IDs whose tokens IAP accepts for programmatic console requests. IAP rejects any client not owned by a project of this project's organization ("not in the same organization as resource"), so the run module refuses such clients at plan time; Google's public clients (32555940559…, 764086051850-…) never pass. Set SWESIM_IAP_PROGRAMMATIC_CLIENTS in the env file (comma-separated) and re-run make tfvars; clearing it clears the key.
iap_programmatic_client_projects [] Project numbers in the same organization whose OAuth clients may appear above besides this project's own
evaluators [] Emails that see evaluator-only material (SWESIM_EVALUATORS)
temporal_address, temporal_namespace "" Temporal Cloud endpoint and namespace (non-secret)
stakeholder_url "" Stakeholder service base URL (Modal)
spend_cap_usd null SWESIM_SPEND_CAP_USD; null = unset
pool_instances {authoring=2, build=2, trials=1, control=1} Instances per worker pool
github_repository "" owner/name trusted by the WIF provider
deploy_workloads true false only for the bootstrap apply (before secrets and image exist)
bucket_name "" → swesim-<project>-workspace Record bucket name
bucket_force_destroy false Let destroy delete the record (PURGE)
sql_tier, sql_deletion_protection db-custom-2-7680, false Cloud SQL sizing / Terraform-side protection
console_min_instances, console_max_instances 1, 3 Console scaling
worker_cpu, worker_memory "1", "2Gi" Per pool instance
notification_channels [] Monitoring channels for the crash-loop alert

The non-secret values come from your env file: make tfvars runs scripts/cloud/tfvars_from_env.py, which writes the git-ignored infra/env.auto.tfvars.json (Temporal address/namespace, stakeholder URL, iap_members/evaluators from gcloud config get account, github_repository from git remote get-url origin) and uploads a copy to the state bucket for CI. infra/terraform.tfvars.example shows the same values for a hand-written terraform.tfvars (git-ignored).

Outputs (infra/outputs.tf; make outputs → git-ignored infra/outputs.json)

project, region, bucket, worker_service_account, deployer_service_account, artifact_repo, sql_connection_name, database_name, database_user, console_url, console_service, iap_audience (/projects/<number>/locations/<region>/services/swesim-console, the JWT audience the console verifies), worker_pools (queue → pool name), wif_provider, image, image_digest, tfstate_bucket, temporal_address, temporal_namespace, github_repository. scripts/cloud/verify_cloud.sh and scripts/cloud/pull.sh read outputs.json.

How to deploy

Prerequisites: a project with billing, gcloud authenticated as an owner (gcloud auth login; gcloud auth application-default login is preferred for Terraform — without it the Makefile falls back to the active account's short-lived token through GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN), Terraform ≥ 1.9, uv, an env file filled from .env.example with SWESIM_ENV_FILE pointing at it, and ~/.modal.toml (or MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET in the env file).

make check                                   # uv sync + offline suite: the checkout is healthy before any spend
make cloud-bootstrap PROJECT=<id> REGION=us-central1 SWESIM_ENV_FILE=<path> [EXTRA_ENV_FILES=<path with OPENROUTER_API_KEY>]

cloud-bootstrap is idempotent and runs, in order: scripts/cloud/bootstrap.sh (enable APIs, create the state bucket, terraform init), make tfvars, terraform apply -var deploy_workloads=false on a stack without workloads (an existing module.run is preserved), make push-secrets (values streamed to Secret Manager on stdin; prints NAME: updated|unchanged), make bootstrap-namespace (scripts/cloud/bootstrap_namespace.py: the six Keyword search attributes every swesim workflow carries, registered idempotently through the SDK's OperatorService; Temporal Cloud refuses that path, so on a fresh Cloud namespace the script prints the exact tcld namespace search-attributes add … command and the UI step for the missing ones and exits 2 — do it once, re-run, and it exits 0), make seed-registry (the tracked registry.json into an empty bucket, never overwriting), make pin-image (scripts/cloud/build.sh: Cloud Build of git archive HEAD, reused when that sha already has an image, digest written to the git-ignored infra/image.auto.tfvars.json), terraform apply (now pinned to the digest), make write-pin (the applied digest read back from Terraform, written to the pin file and published to the state bucket), make migrate (swesim index migrate when the command exists and Cloud SQL is reachable, otherwise a notice), and scripts/cloud/verify_cloud.sh. Because the digest lives in image.auto.tfvars.json, a later plain make apply keeps the pools on it (it never reverts to :latest); -var image=... on the command line still overrides.

The pin guard. make apply first runs scripts/cloud/pin_guard.py, which compares the pin file with the image the four pools and the console run and refuses the apply when they disagree: a stale laptop file after a GitHub deploy (mismatch), no pin file on a fresh clone while the pools run a digest (pin-missing, the apply would roll them to :latest), pools that disagree with each other (mixed), or gcloud unable to list them (unknown). make pull-pin adopts the pin the last deploy published to gs://<project>-swesim-tfstate/image.auto.tfvars.json (make push-pin uploads the local one); FORCE_PIN=1 records the disagreement and applies anyway. make deploy and make cloud-bootstrap set FORCE_PIN=1 for the apply that follows their own pin-image — rolling is their purpose — and then run write-pin, so the laptop file, the bucket copy and the pools always name the digest that was applied. Both deploy paths publish the same object, so either side can pick up where the other left off.

Later deploys:

make deploy SHA=<sha>        # build that commit -> terraform apply pinned to its digest -> write-pin -> migrate -> verify-cloud
make push-secrets            # after rotating a value in the env file (only changed secrets get a new version)
make pull-pin                # adopt the digest the last deploy (laptop or GitHub) published before a plain apply
make plan | make apply       # any Terraform change; apply is refused while the pin disagrees with the pools (FORCE_PIN=1 overrides)
make pull                    # mirror the record (without trials/*/task/) into the laptop workspace

Every apply is expected to be clean on re-run (No changes.); the second apply of the bootstrap night is saved as terraform-apply-2.txt under the evidence directory.

The GitHub path (.github/workflows/deploy.yml)

The CI deployer applies changes inside module.run only. A plan that changes IAM, SQL, bucket settings, logging or other infrastructure is rejected before apply; an authenticated project operator applies those changes with make apply. The deploy checks out and tests the requested commit, requires a pinned build digest, and uses the same Temporal connection for its open-execution check and final verification. A missing open-execution command stops deployment. After the apply it publishes the applied digest as gs://<project>-swesim-tfstate/image.auto.tfvars.json; a laptop runs make pull-pin before its next plain make apply (the pin guard refuses a stale pin otherwise).

workflow_dispatch (inputs sha, override_open_executions) or a v* tag: authenticates with WIF as swesim-deployer, fetches env.auto.tfvars.json from the state bucket, runs the open-executions check (uv run swesim workflows open-types; a listed type blocks the deploy unless the override is set and recorded; skipped with a warning while the command is not in the checkout), builds the image, plans and applies with the digest, runs verify_cloud.sh and posts digest, plan line and verify output as the job summary. Repository variables, set once after the first apply (gh authenticated):

gh variable set GCP_PROJECT --body "$(terraform -chdir=infra output -raw project)"
gh variable set GCP_REGION  --body "$(terraform -chdir=infra output -raw region)"
gh variable set WIF_PROVIDER --body "$(terraform -chdir=infra output -raw wif_provider)"
gh variable set DEPLOYER_SA  --body "$(terraform -chdir=infra output -raw deployer_service_account)"

(make gh-variables runs exactly these.) ci.yml runs the offline suite, the contract tests, ruff --select E9,F, terraform fmt -check and terraform validate on every push and pull request.

Reaching the index from outside Cloud Run

The instance has no authorized networks and no VPC path. From a laptop use the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy (cloud-sql-proxy <sql_connection_name> with roles/cloudsql.client) and SWESIM_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://swesim:<DB_PASSWORD>@127.0.0.1:5432/swesim, or run swesim index migrate | rebuild | status as a one-off Cloud Run Job with the worker image, the swesim-worker account, the Cloud SQL connection and the SWESIM_DATABASE_URL secret (the same shape as a trial Job).

How to destroy

make cloud-destroy PROJECT=<id>          # everything except the record bucket and the state bucket
make cloud-destroy PROJECT=<id> PURGE=1  # also deletes the record bucket and its objects

Without PURGE=1 the workspace bucket is removed from the state first (so it is retained), then terraform destroy runs. A later cloud-bootstrap on the same project must adopt the retained bucket: make import-bucket. The state bucket is never deleted by these targets. Caveats: Cloud SQL instance names are reserved for about a week after deletion (the instance carries a random suffix for this reason); WIF pool/provider ids are soft-deleted for 30 days (gcloud iam workload-identity-pools undelete to reuse them).

Applied by hand

Nothing is applied by hand. Two things are deliberately outside Terraform: the state bucket (scripts/cloud/bootstrap.sh, gcloud storage buckets create + versioning) and the secret values (scripts/cloud/push_secrets.py). Trial Jobs are runtime resources of the launcher.

Layout

infra/
  versions.tf providers.tf variables.tf main.tf outputs.tf   root module (partial GCS backend, configured at init)
  terraform.tfvars.example                                    the non-secret inputs, with placeholders
  modules/registry  Artifact Registry
  modules/storage   record bucket + Cloud Build source bucket
  modules/sql       Cloud SQL instance, database, user, generated password
  modules/secrets   Secret Manager resources (+ the two Terraform-written versions)
  modules/iam       service accounts, roles, WIF pool/provider, IAP service agent
  modules/run       worker pools, console service, IAP bindings
  modules/logging   log-based metrics and the crash-loop alert
scripts/cloud/
  bootstrap.sh build.sh push_secrets.py tfvars_from_env.py pin_guard.py bootstrap_namespace.py verify_cloud.sh pull.sh
  (import_vm.sh: storage stream)
Dockerfile.worker  cloudbuild.yaml  .dockerignore  .gcloudignore  Makefile  .github/workflows/{ci,deploy}.yml
